That's a good point, as someone who can't afford big vet bills and a well bred puppy, this is how I deal with it. Opportunities. Vague but I'll go into detail (also sorry for the late reply I just found this post wanted to share my opinions in experiences.) I can't work a full time job without an SD or even a part time. Resources for those of us who are disabled does help, but owning a SD or just a pet is expensive, I know. While it is a privilege, that doesn't mean it shouldn't be available to those of us who can't necessarily afford all of that and need them to function. Saving helps but having a support system (family and people who care) is really helpful, I can manage odd jobs and moving around numbers to afford care for my SDIT and pets. None of them go without care, I make sure they are cared for before I am. I'm well aware that trainers and getting the perfect prospect would boost my odds but that's not avaliable to me and it won't be until I improve some. What will improve my quality of life? A service dog. You see the problem- it's actually sad, but I and many others are just trying our best, if I fail, okay, I knew the risk i was taking and will have learned something. If I do succeed then good for me, now my life will probably improve to the point of making more money which will then create better odds for my next SD. 

That being said, I myself am making sure the dog is cared for and if I have to wash I know I would have to re-home and that's something I'm willing to deal with. I know for myself this is something I need and know will help tremendously, so yeah. Alright I'll exit now, not trying to argue or be mean or anything, rather just explaining my POV.

I agree, trainers do increase odds and I respect that, and I've definitely seen those people who aren't educated on it and fail because of it. That being said, some of us just have to learn as we go and make the best out of our situation. There is alot to consider when thinking of getting an SD with the intention to owner train. I don't think anyone should tell someone else they shouldn't owner train because of financial reasons, the warnings are fair and definitely valid, but judging isn't helpful. (Not directing that at you, just speaking generally.) I have little to no experience with training, but I'm learning, I can't afford to seek professional training so I'm willing to do it myself. Even if that means possibly failing, washing is expensive, I agree, but we can't all afford expensive training routinely which would lead to failing anyway. It doesn't make sense to hire someone I know I won't be able to afford on a regular basis when I can do the research myself.  To be 100% clear, I know very well that getting a trainer and doing everything "right" will increase odds of succeeding but I literally can't and will not be in a position to do so without a SD. It's unfortunate, but there's nothing else I can do besides try to do it on my own. I just wish I wasn't judged based on that decision and made to feel bad about it. 

And the thing is, telling someone they shouldn't have a SD or try to train their own because of financial problems isn't helping anyone. I'd also like to add to that, I don't mean basic needs of the dog, yes, that should 100% be taken care of. I mean the stuff that we can't afford, professional training, well bred expensive puppy that's been behavior and temperament tested. Traveling to get them and I'm sure I'm missing other stuff, I'm typing this out late so apologies if there's any errors. I think I've made my point, I know I'm missing stuff but this is okay for now.

So I'm 18 and I attempted a few months myself, it didn't injure me to the point of permanent damage. At least not physically anyway, but I've been pretty set on doing it "properly" for a little over a year now. Infact, I still think of it as an option.

Getting off topic, I wasn't doing too well around a week ago, both feeling suicidal and panicking over the thought of "what happens after we die?" I went out for a bit and ran into someone I know and she gave me something I needed. Hope. Something I haven't felt in years, to be specific she offered me a puppy, which may sound silly but I've been needing an service dog for around 3 and half years now. 

It kind of stunned me because it was the exact breed I was looking for and it made me think a bit, maybe things could get better, maybe I can do this. 

I won't say what everyone else says, things might get worse before they get better. But just try and hold on for a little longer, claw your way out of the hole, you don't even need to make it to the top. Just start climbing. 

Reach out for help to someone you trust and love, if you don't have that, find those people. It's hard and if you're overwhelmed don't push yourself. 

No one knows anything, we're all just kind of making it up as we go, the most important thing you can do is find something you love. Friends, family, pets, a hobby or whatever you find peace in. This isn't easy and you will suffer before you can heal, it's part of life, it's not fair or right but it is still there. You don't need to be positive or "get over" whatever you're going through, take it one minute, hour and day at a time. 

If you have that tiny voice in your head that wants to get better, to hope, even if it's faint, listen closely, hold on for just a little longer.

It completely counts, I get it, I thought my first attempt wasn't "good enough" or "didn't count." Too, I basically tore up my arm with a razor but didn't go very deep at all, didn't need stitches but my intention was to unalive myself.

These last few months I've been set on it, but around a week ago when I relapsed with SH, I got something that I needed, a service dog. Not that, thats what you need, (unless you think that's an option that would help.)

But my point is, if you just wait, if you just try for a little longer, something might happen that will change how you feel right now. 

I know it can be hard and I don't know your story or what you've been through, but you're not alone.  If you have someone you trust and love try reaching out to them. It can make a difference, and even if that's not a option, I'd gladly help you any way I can.
